paragraphs: fav_count: 355 of 355 rows have known values (100.0% coverage).

At k = 50, known anchor–neighbor pairs differ by 34.62 units on average. The local/global variance ratio is 0.8963 and Moran’s I is 0.1169. These describe similarity of nearby values, not prediction accuracy.
Known-neighbor coverage at this k is 100.0%. Unknown neighbors are excluded from agreement denominators; missing annotations can bias the result.

The saved null comparison gives an empirical one-sided p-value of 0.1667 for mean_neighbor_abs_difference. This tests the specified shuffle, not semantic understanding; use the combined multiple-testing table and practical effect sizes when judging the finding.
The probe panel measures recoverability on a held-out split. Compare each model with its baseline; recoverability and nearest-neighbor usefulness answer different questions.
